title: Lecturer on Restorative Dentistry and Biomaterials Sciences
bio: Dr. Elizabeth Shin Perry is a lecturer on restorative dentistry and biomaterials sciences at the Harvard School of Dental Medicine (HSDM) and a clinical instructor in the Advanced Graduate Program in Endodontics. She earned a Bachelor of Science from the University of Pennsylvania and graduated cum laude from HSDM with a Doctor of Dental Medicine degree before completing a postdoctoral certificate in endodontics at the University of Connecticut. Perry serves as president-elect of the American Association of Endodontists and has previously held leadership roles, including vice president, treasurer, secretary, and District I director. She also served on the American Dental Association Code Maintenance Committee and is author of the endodontics chapter in the ADA Coding Companion . Perry is a diplomate of the American Board of Endodontics and a fellow of the International College of Dentists. At HSDM, she received the Outstanding Faculty Award from Harvard endodontic residents and has served as chair of the Endodontic Faculty Search Committee and on the admissions committee for Advanced Graduate Education in Endodontics. Her scholarly work focuses on immature teeth, regenerative and surgical endodontics, traumatic dental injuries, and tooth preservation. She has published and lectured extensively nationally and internationally and is co-editor and chapter author of Pitt Ford’s Problem-Based Learning in Endodontology . With more than 30 years of clinical experience, Perry maintains a private practice limited to endodontics in Westfield, Massachusetts, while remaining active in education, organized dentistry, advocacy, and patient-centered care.
